This enables probabilistic comparisons across matchups, where the difference between tiers becomes a proxy for expected margin of victory. The rookie performance primitive integrates historical debut data to project future contributions, using a kernel-based regression that accounts for era-specific scaling. Edge rusher production is derived from a composite score of pass-rush success and run-defense contribution, which informs high-leverage defensive selections. These primitives are interlinked through shared temporal and spatial dimensions—each is grounded in observed game data and can be updated via Bayesian inference. Failure modes include overfitting to small samples, misalignment of metrics across eras, and incorrect assumptions about team or player stability.
